## Summary

A publishing panel explains changes in discovery, editorial labor, rights and author compensation, with Eisman mainly asking questions. The material themes are platform dependence, AI substitution of generic information, differentiated author brands and licensing economics. Verified corrections concern Amazon's generated-content policy, the distinction between training and piracy in Bartz, and author-funded costs hidden by headline hybrid royalty comparisons.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

- [Bartz v Anthropic order on fair use, document 231](https://www.loeb.com/-/media/files/pdfs/2025-pdfs/ip-entertainment-pdfs/bartz-v-anthropic.pdf) (2025-06-23): Court distinguished transformative model training from acquisition and retention of pirated books. Training use received summary judgment; pirated library copies were not excused by that later use.
- [Copyright and Artificial Intelligence initiative](https://www.copyright.gov/ai/index.html) (2025 reports, inspected2026-11-10): Office issued reports addressing digital replicas, copyrightability and generative-AI training. Copyright in human authorship and licensing/fair-use questions require separate analysis; policy study is not a blanket court judgment.

Conditional reasoning: Total portfolio profit is the sum of title profits and losses, so the portfolio can be profitable even when many titles lose money.

## Framework and tools

- Follow distribution and discovery power as formats change.
- Separate generic information from differentiated author voice and community.
- Do not infer legal infringement merely from technical model training.
- Compare net contract economics after author-funded costs and rights grants.
- Use portfolio economics for hit-driven creative businesses.
- Historical data can screen out ideas with no close precedent.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Print, ebook and audio revenue versus unit shares
- Title portfolio profit distribution
- Advance, royalty and author-funded cost comparison
- Training rights versus output and acquisition rights
- Launch demand versus backlist discovery
